title: Finite projective coordinate reindexing preserves the twisting module
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $\beta$ a finite nonempty coordinate type. For projective space with its base-change integral-model convention [def-pc-proj] and twisting module [def-pc-projective-space-twist], there are $n\ge0$ and a scheme isomorphism $e:\mathbb P(\beta;S)\cong\mathbb P(\operatorname{ULift}(\operatorname{Fin}(n+1));S)$ over $S$ such that $e^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\mathcal O(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback].

source.place: Constructions Definition 01NF and Lemma 01NE: projective-space charts and coordinate construction, applied to bijective renaming and its inverse.

proof.text: Choose n+1 equal to the cardinality of beta and a coordinate bijection. Polynomial variable renaming and its inverse preserve grading and coefficients.

Rename each standard chart and its degree-zero localization. The affine scheme isomorphisms agree on overlaps since they preserve all coordinate ratios; glue them and their inverses, and then base change the integral-model isomorphism to S.

The maps preserve constants, hence are over S. Send each rank-one twist basis to its renamed basis; preservation of coordinate-ratio transition units makes these isomorphisms glue. The result is the pullback of O(1) along e.
